prompt.context: A friend of mine is super rich and is always looking into interesting investment opportunities. To raise funds for renovation, Ferris Wheel management in Chicago is considering inviting bids from High Net Worth Individuals (HNIs) to let them run the Wheel for a whole year, 7 years later. As a fan of Chicago and the Wheel, my friend wants to bid on this opportunity.
prompt.question: How should your friend think about whether and how much to bid on the opportunity to run the Chicago Ferris Wheel for one year, starting 7 years from now?

clarifying_info.q: What ROI does your friend require?
Would your friend be involved in operations?
clarifying_info.a: Yes — if the bid is won, your friend would be CEO and run the operations

clarifying_info.q: Does your friend have any relevant business interests?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, your friend has some interesting investments in the food and beverage space

framework: Revenue analysis: ticket sales (price, capacity, utilization, seasonality) and other revenues (F&B, memorabilia, advertising, synergies)
Cost analysis: salaries/labor, marketing, rent, energy, maintenance, insurance
Capabilities to operate: relevant experience, hiring needs, management bandwidth
Risk factors: 7-year forecast uncertainty, competitive/market changes, opportunity cost of capital
Funding: ability to secure bid capital and bidding strategy

questions.prompt: Brainstorm how you would calculate ticket revenues — what key inputs do you need?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify: ticket price, hourly capacity of the wheel, hours of operation per day, number of operating days, and utilization rate. Strong candidates will also note the need to segment by season (spring/summer/fall vs. winter) and by day type (weekday vs. weekend) to capture pricing premiums and utilization differences.

questions.prompt: How would you think about pricing tickets?
questions.guidance: Strong answers include: weekend/holiday peak pricing premium; seasonal variation (lower footfall in Chicago winters, heavy crowds in summer); combined packages (e.g., F&B + ride); multi-ride passes; corporate/group rates.

questions.prompt: What other revenue streams could the Ferris Wheel generate beyond ticket sales?
questions.guidance: Good answers include: food & beverage sales, photo memories/souvenir photos, private cabin rentals, memorabilia/merchandise, advertising partnerships (on cabins, fencing, digital), synergy revenue from friend's existing F&B investments.

questions.prompt: Now calculate annual ticket revenue using the following data: the wheel runs 52 weeks, 11 hours/day, capacity 200 people/hour, base ticket price $15 (weekends carry a 30% premium). Utilization: Spring/Summer/Fall weekdays 80%, weekends 100%; Winter weekdays 50%, weekends 75%. Assume 26 weeks Spring/Summer/Fall and 26 weeks Winter. Other revenues including synergy benefits total $4.5M.
questions.guidance: Candidate should build a 2x2 matrix: season (Spring/Summer/Fall vs. Winter) x day-type (weekday vs. weekend). Weekend ticket price = $15 x 1.30 = $20. Steps per cell: days -> operating hours -> utilized hours -> riders -> revenue. Sum all four cells plus $4.5M other revenues to reach total ~$14M.

math.setup: 2x2 matrix: {Spring/Summer/Fall, Winter} x {Weekday, Weekend}. Weekend price = $15 * 1.30 = $20.
steps: Spring/Summer/Fall Weekday: 26 wks x 5 days = 130 days; 130 x 11 hrs = 1,430 hrs; x 80% util = 1,144 hrs; x 200 ppl/hr = 228,800 riders; x $15 = $3.432M
Spring/Summer/Fall Weekend: 26 wks x 2 days = 52 days; 52 x 11 hrs = 572 hrs; x 100% util = 572 hrs; x 200 ppl/hr = 114,400 riders; x $20 = $2.288M
Winter Weekday: 26 wks x 5 days = 130 days; 130 x 11 hrs = 1,430 hrs; x 50% util = 715 hrs; x 200 ppl/hr = 143,000 riders; x $15 = $2.145M
Winter Weekend: 26 wks x 2 days = 52 days; 52 x 11 hrs = 572 hrs; x 75% util = 429 hrs; x 200 ppl/hr = 85,800 riders; x $20 = $1.716M
Total revenues = $9.521M ticket sales + $4.5M other = $14.021M, rounded to $14M

questions.prompt: Brainstorm the costs of running the Ferris Wheel for a year.
questions.guidance: Good cost categories: salaries and labor (operators, security, ticketing staff), marketing, rent/lease, energy/utilities, maintenance and repairs, insurance. The casebook provides total annual costs of $3M — candidate should accept and proceed once a reasonable list is generated.

questions.prompt: Given revenues of $14M and total costs of $3M, calculate net income and the maximum bid amount your friend should make today to achieve a 10% ROI.
questions.guidance: Step 1: Net income = $14M - $3M = $11M. Step 2: Apply time-value discounting — cash is earned 7 years from now. Rule of 72: 72 / 10% = ~7.2 years to double money, so $11M earned in 7 years is worth roughly $11M / 2 = $5.5M in today's dollars. Step 3: For exactly 10% ROI, the max bid today = NPV / (1 + ROI) = $5.5M / 1.10 = $5M. Strong candidates proactively raise discounting; weaker candidates need prompting.

math.setup: Net income = Revenues - Costs; NPV via Rule of 72 (double in ~7 years at 10%); Max bid = NPV / 1.10
steps: Rule of 72: 72 / 10 = 7.2 years to double => money doubles in ~7 years => NPV = $11M / 2 = $5.5M

brainstorming.prompt: What are the key revenue streams beyond basic ticket sales for a Ferris Wheel?

categories.name: Synergies
ideas: Exclusive F&B concession rights leveraging existing supplier relationships

recommendation: Make a bid for a maximum of $5M to ensure the required 10% ROI is achieved (NPV of $5.5M in today's dollars)
Any bid below $5M would yield an ROI above 10%, improving the investment outcome
risks: Revenue and cost projections may not hold constant over 7 years; market trends, competition, and consumer preferences could shift
Your friend has no prior experience managing a large public attraction; consider whether to hire an experienced CEO instead of serving in that role
Opportunity cost: are there other investments available with expected returns greater than 10%? The bid should be evaluated against the best alternative use of capital
7-year macroeconomic and regulatory changes in Chicago could affect operations
next_steps: Ensure sufficient liquid funds are available to make the bid and cover operating capital
Develop a bidding strategy to win the auction at a price below the $5M maximum, maximizing effective ROI
Identify synergy-creating investments in F&B or adjacent spaces to make over the next few years to boost the non-ticket revenue line
Conduct due diligence on the Wheel's existing operations, maintenance history, and any pending regulatory requirements
